stem: A client enrolled in an oncology investigational-drug trial calls the research nurse between scheduled visits to report a new severe symptom. Which action best reflects the oncology clinical research nurse's role?

options.A: Assess and document the symptom, promptly notify the investigator/research team, follow the protocol-defined safety and adverse-event pathway, and coordinate clinically necessary care.
options.B: Independently reduce the investigational-drug dose before contacting the investigator so treatment can continue without a protocol interruption.
options.C: Wait until the next scheduled study visit to document the symptom unless the client independently decides to seek emergency care.
options.D: Omit the symptom from study documentation if it is already listed as a known adverse effect of the investigational drug.

rationale: Oncology clinical research nursing requires precise protocol adherence, adverse-event monitoring and reporting, rigorous documentation, and coordination of care. When a participant reports a new severe symptom, the research nurse should assess and document the event, promptly involve the investigator/research team, and use the study protocol's safety and reporting procedures while coordinating clinically necessary care. FDA regulations place responsibility on the investigator for conducting the study according to the investigational plan, protecting participants, maintaining accurate case histories, and reporting relevant adverse effects. A nurse should not independently alter an investigational regimen outside the protocol and delegated authority, delay evaluation of a severe symptom until a routine visit, or omit a known/expected event from required trial documentation.
educational_objective: Apply the oncology clinical research nurse's role to a participant-reported adverse event by prioritizing assessment, accurate documentation, protocol adherence, prompt investigator communication, and coordinated safety care within delegated scope.
source_organization: Oncology Nursing Society (ONS); U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
source_document_title: Ready to Manage Clinical Trials? Here’s How to Grow Your Competence From Novice to Expert; Federal Regulations for Clinical Investigators; Investigator Responsibilities – Safety Reporting for Investigational Drugs and Devices
source_version_date: ONS 2026-01-15; FDA regulations page published 2026; FDA final safety-reporting guidance 2025-12
source_locator: ONS 2026 article — paragraphs describing precise protocol adherence, adverse-event monitoring/reporting, rigorous documentation and care coordination; FDA 21 CFR 312.60, 312.62 and 312.64; FDA December 2025 final guidance overview
source_claim_supported: ONS identifies protocol adherence, adverse-event monitoring/reporting, documentation and care coordination as core clinical research nursing responsibilities. FDA requires investigators to conduct IND studies according to the investigational plan, protect participant safety, maintain adequate and accurate case histories, and promptly report qualifying adverse effects; delegated nursing work remains within protocol and investigator oversight.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — interdisciplinary collaboration, continuity/coordination of care, client rights, informed participation, and safe assignment/delegation within scope
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — clinical-trial care coordination, protocol adherence, and participant safety
correction_summary: Upgraded the original role-definition item into an applied investigational-drug safety scenario. Replaced the generic ONS homepage with current 2026 ONS clinical-research nursing guidance plus current FDA investigator regulations and December 2025 safety-reporting guidance. Clarified that the research nurse assesses, documents, coordinates and follows protocol while promptly involving the investigator, rather than independently changing the investigational regimen or suppressing expected adverse-event documentation.
audit_findings: Original item was a low-discrimination role-definition question with vague, obviously incorrect distractors.
Current ONS guidance directly identifies protocol adherence, adverse-event monitoring/reporting, rigorous documentation and care coordination as clinical research nurse responsibilities.

FDA regulations and current safety-reporting guidance preserve investigator accountability and support prompt evaluation/documentation/reporting rather than unsupervised nursing alteration of the investigational regimen.
The final item avoids implying that expected adverse events may be omitted from required study records or deferred until a routine visit.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct response with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported scope expansion, or unresolved source conflict.
